skill.name: executor-planning
skill.description: Turn approved specifications into implementable tasks, or repair existing plans with explicit interfaces, tests, requirement coverage, and dependencies.
skill.summary: Convert approved specifications into self-contained implementation tasks with interfaces, tests, dependencies, and human-approved execution handoff.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: Most of the 221 static findings are Markdown formatting, legitimate companion references, or routine planning commands. Two temporary-file findings remain confirmed, and a semantic finding identifies overly broad Git staging. No evidence found of prompt injection or exfiltration; companion script implementations are outside the reviewed package.

remediation.issue: Brief verification writes and reads a predictable shared temporary file.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mktemp, stop on extraction failure, and read only successfully generated briefs. Clean up with a trap.

remediation.issue: Directory-wide Git staging can include unrelated initiative files.
remediation.suggestion: Stage only the reviewed plan, index, and specification files. Inspect the staged diff and scan every staged file for secrets before committing.

content.user_title: Turn Approved Specifications into Implementation Plans
content.value_statement: Incomplete implementation plans leave developers guessing about interfaces, dependencies, and acceptance criteria. This skill structures approved specifications into traceable tasks with explicit tests and execution gates.
actual_capabilities: Structure plans with frontmatter, constraints, interfaces, file maps, dependency maps, and numbered task identifiers.
Split specifications into independently testable plans with explicit ordering and predecessor assumptions.
Map requirement identifiers to tasks and repeat relevant constraints inside each task brief.
Specify test-driven task steps with exact commands, expected failures, passing results, and refactoring checks.
Guide verification using companion tools for task extraction, plan linting, store checks, and secret scanning.
Prepare regression review, document cross-links, and a human choice between subagent and inline execution.
limitations: Requires an approved specification, a decided decomposition session, and interface documents for work spanning components.
Companion Executor skills, reference documents, and scripts are not included in this single-file package.
Provides planning instructions rather than a standalone implementation engine or guaranteed validation results.
Includes shared temporary-file and broad Git-staging examples that require safer handling before use.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Reviewable Delivery Plan
use_cases.description: Convert an approved feature specification into traceable tasks with explicit file ownership, interfaces, and acceptance tests.

use_cases.title: Create Self-Contained Agent Briefs
use_cases.description: Prepare tasks that isolated coding agents can implement without access to the surrounding conversation or complete plan.

use_cases.title: Repair a Multi-Plan Handoff
use_cases.description: Find missing requirement coverage, interface mismatches, dependency cycles, and incomplete test steps before implementation begins.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a draft implementation plan from [approved specification] and [interface document]. Check prerequisites and identify missing inputs before drafting tasks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: translate an approved specification into a first plan.

prompt_templates.title: Define Testable Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Refine [draft plan] into self-contained tasks. Include requirement IDs, exact interfaces, file lists, failing tests, expected results, and refactoring steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve task detail before dispatch.

prompt_templates.title: Split an Approved Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [decided decomposition session] to split [approved specification] into independently testable plans. Document coverage, predecessor assumptions, execution order, and dependency maps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan delivery across multiple components.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Repair the Plan Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [plan set] against [specification] and [interface contracts]. Repair coverage gaps, dependency cycles, and extraction defects. Report unavailable validation tools without claiming success.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a plan set for regression review and human execution approval.

output_examples.input: Plan an approved feature that adds scoring and routing through documented interfaces.
output: Draft plan: scoring and routing, with requirement coverage and exact interface contracts.
Task sequence: define shared types, implement scoring, then integrate routing.
Dependency map: routing consumes shared types and scoring results.
Acceptance checks: explicit expected values, negative-input tests, and repeatable test commands.
Handoff: complete plan regression before asking the human to select an execution mode.

output_examples.input: Review a draft plan whose final task contains a dependency section and omits an expected test failure.
output: Extraction defect: move the dependency section above the first task heading.
Test defect: name the exact expected failure before implementation exists.
Coverage check: associate every requirement with at least one task.
Verification status: rerun task extraction and plan linting with the companion tools before claiming the gate passed.

best_practices: Confirm specification approval, interface contracts, and the human-selected decomposition before drafting tasks.
Make each task independently understandable with exact requirements, interfaces, tests, and dependency references.
Verify companion tools, use private temporary files, and inspect explicitly staged changes before the execution handoff.
anti_patterns: Inventing interfaces or architectural decisions inside an implementation plan.
Using placeholders, implicit constraints, or references to another task instead of a complete acceptance contract.
Starting implementation before regression clears and the human selects an execution mode.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The workflow still requires the companion Executor resources and project documents.

faq.question: What inputs are required before planning?
faq.answer: Provide an approved specification, relevant architecture decisions, and a decided decomposition session. Work spanning components also requires interface documents.

faq.question: Does this package include the validation scripts?
faq.answer: No. This package contains only the planning instructions. The referenced scripts and supporting documents belong to the companion Executor package.

faq.question: Can the skill invent missing interfaces?
faq.answer: No. Missing interfaces require an architecture decision before planning resumes. Task signatures must match the approved interface document.

faq.question: When does implementation begin?
faq.answer: Implementation begins after plan regression clears and the human chooses subagent or inline execution. Planning does not authorize implementation by itself.

faq.question: What security precautions apply to the examples?
faq.answer: Replace the shared temporary pathname with a private temporary directory. Stage only reviewed files and inspect staged changes before committing.
